text.en: Change the last message so it says how old they are now.
Ask for the sender's name and print "From" and their name at the end.
Also print how many months old they are (age × 12).

brief.en: Ask for a pet's name and its age in years, then print its age in "dog years" (age × 7).

text.en: Make it work with decimal measurements such as 2.5.
Print the units (cm) after each answer.
Also work out the area of a triangle with the same width and height.

brief.en: Ask for the length of one side of a square, then print its area and perimeter.

text.en: Delete the line temp = a and use b = a instead. What goes wrong?
Add c = 5 and rotate the values so a gets b's value, b gets c's and c gets a's.
Replace the three swapping lines with a, b = b, a.

brief.en: Ask for two words and print them in the opposite order.

text.en: Change the joining age to 11.
Say "year" instead of "years" when there is only one year to wait.
Turn away anyone over 18 with a different message.

brief.en: Ask how many hours of sleep someone had and tell them whether it was enough (8 or more).

text.en: Add an A* grade for 90 and above.
Also print "Well done!" for grades A and B.
Print an error message instead of a grade if the score is above 100.

brief.en: Ask for the temperature in °C and print "cold" (below 10), "mild" (10 to 20) or "hot" (above 20).

text.en: Accept the password whatever capital letters are used (hint: .lower()).
Add a second password that also works.
When the password is wrong, say how many characters were typed (hint: len()).

brief.en: Ask a quiz question, then say whether the answer is right or wrong.

text.en: Make the numbers start from 0 instead of 1.
Print the name in capital letters (hint: name.upper()).
After the loop, print "That's a lot!" only if times is more than 5.

brief.en: Ask for a word and a number, then print the word that many times on one line (hint: print(word, end=" ")).

text.en: Make it go up to 12 x.
Make it count down from 12 to 1.
Only print the lines where the answer is even.

brief.en: Print the square of each number from 1 to 10.

text.en: Start the countdown from 10.
Count down in twos.
Ask the user which number to start from.

brief.en: Count up from 1 to a number the user types, then print "Ready or not, here I come!"

text.en: Ask how many items there are before the loop, and loop that many times.
Give a discount of 10 off if the total is over 50.
Only print the total once, at the end.

brief.en: Ask for 5 test scores and print their average.

text.en: Change the secret number.
Say "try" instead of "tries" when it is guessed first time.
Stop after 5 wrong guesses and reveal the number.

brief.en: Keep asking for a password until the right one is typed, then print "Welcome".

text.en: Make it stop once the value passes 1000.
Triple the value each time instead of doubling it.
Ask the user for the starting value.

brief.en: Start with 100 and keep halving it until it is less than 1, counting the steps.

text.en: Add a menu option c that prints a joke.
Print "I don't understand" for any other choice.
Count how many choices were made and print the count at the end.

brief.en: Write a calculator menu: keep asking for two numbers and add them until the user types "stop".

text.en: Let the user add 5 items.
Print the list in alphabetical order (hint: items.sort()).
Don't add an item if it is already in the list.

brief.en: Ask for the names of 4 friends, then print them in reverse order.

text.en: Find the lowest score instead.
Also add up all the scores and print the total.
Count how many scores are over 25.

brief.en: Make a list of 5 temperatures and print how many are below freezing (0).

text.en: Add a third rectangle and include it in the total.
Write a perimeter(width, height) function and use it too.
Ask the user for the width and height of one rectangle.

brief.en: Write a function that converts miles to kilometres (× 1.6) and use it for three distances.

text.en: Check the numbers 1 to 10.
Write is_multiple_of_3(number) and use it as well.
Count how many even numbers there were and print the count.

brief.en: Write a function that returns the larger of two numbers, and test it with three pairs.

text.en: Print the total as well as the average.
Also print the highest score.
Add your own name and score to scores.txt in the Files tab, then run it again.

brief.en: Make a file called temps.txt with one temperature on each line, then write a program that reads it and prints the highest and lowest temperatures.

text.en: Number each guest in the list (1. Ada, 2. Alan, …).
Also ask for a message and save it on the same line as the name, e.g. "Sam: Hello!".
Change "a" to "w" on line 2 and run it twice. What happens to the other names, and why?

brief.en: Ask for a score and add it to a file called highscores.txt, then print every score saved so far.

text.en: Add two more colours to the list.
Read colours.txt back in and print each colour in capitals (hint: .upper()).
Write each colour's position too, like 1,red, so the file is a CSV.

brief.en: Ask for five words, save them to words.txt (one on each line), then read the file and print the words in reverse order.

text.en: Count how many times the word "the" appears, whatever its capitals.
Write the three results to a file called report.txt as well as printing them.
Change poem.txt in the Files tab to a short poem of your own and run it again.

brief.en: Read a file of names (one on each line) and write the names that start with A to a new file called a-names.txt.

text.en: Also print the total of all the scores.
Also print the lowest score, in the same style as the highest.
Change every score in scores.txt to a negative number and run it again. What goes wrong, and how would you fix it?

brief.en: Make a file called temps.txt with one temperature on each line, then write a program that reads it and prints the coldest temperature.

text.en: Change > to >= on line 11. Who is the top scorer now, and why?
Also print who scored lowest, like Bottom scorer: Cai with 11.
Save the class average in summary.txt too, on a second line.

brief.en: Make a file called times.csv with a runner's name and race time in seconds on each line, then write a program that saves the fastest runner to a new file called report.txt and prints the average time.

text.en: Change the program so only scores of 15 or more are saved.
Print each score that doesn't pass, like Failed: 7.
Save the scores that don't pass to a second file called failed.txt.

brief.en: Read scores.txt and write each score doubled to a new file called doubled.txt, then print how many scores were written.

text.en: Print how many places were averaged, like Places: 3.
Also print the warmest temperature, like Warmest: 11.2.
reduce(add, temps) works through the list two values at a time. Write out each step it takes with these three temperatures. Which lines of 11d (c) does it replace?

brief.en: Choose three places you have visited. Use map to get their temperatures and reduce to add them up, then add "dd/mm/yyyy - total of x celsius" to the end of a file called totals.txt.

text.en: Print how many places were averaged, like Places: 3.
Also print the warmest temperature, like Warmest: 11.2.
Compare this program with 11d (c). Which lines replaced the for loop, and why are the places no longer printed?

brief.en: Choose three places you have visited. Use a list comprehension to get their temperatures, then add "dd/mm/yyyy - warmest: x celsius" to the end of a file called warmest.txt.

text.en: Print how many places were averaged, like Places: 3.
Run the program twice. What does temperatures.txt hold now, and why? What would happen if "a" were "w"?
Also print the warmest place, like Warmest: London.

brief.en: Choose three places you have visited. Write a program that finds the coldest of them right now and adds "dd/mm/yyyy - coldest: place" to the end of a file called coldest.txt.

text.en: Make the chatbot reply I love cats too! when a message mentions cats.
Make the chatbot say goodbye and stop when the user types quit, as well as bye.
Type BYE in capitals. Why does the chat still end? Which part of the code makes that happen?

brief.en: Make a chatbot for a café. It asks what you'd like, gives a different answer for tea, coffee and cake, and keeps going until you type done.

text.en: Change the program so it's boiling from 20 °C. Which places get a different message now?
Count how many places are cold and print the count at the end, like Cold places: 2.
Print the warmest place at the end, like Warmest: Hornsea.

brief.en: Make a list of five places you'd like to visit. For each one, print its temperature and whether you'd need a coat (below 15 °C), then print how many places need one.

text.en: Print the squares all the way up to 10 squared.
Print each number's cube too, like 2 cubed is 8.
Ask the user how many squares to print.

brief.en: Write a program that prints the numbers 1 to 10 with each one doubled, like 3 doubled is 6.
